items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: And George Field, he was a very good musician.

ctx.x: Well, as you grew on in years, did you hear any more music?

Oh yeah, I, in spite of me hearing this music, I used to say, the second line just like the rest of the kids. We used to try sometime way away from home, you know, out of the neighborhood. I remember I, I think it was about the 30th of May and some friends of mine and I, we, we came all the way down to French Bar Town and the boys got behind us and ran us all the way to the podgers and ramparts, you know. And so I always did love music. I used to do a lot of whistling. I still do. And so, but I didn't have no…
Where was he from? He's from New Orleans.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Snags, by that time Snags was playing drums and George Field on trombone and he had Busta Bailey and on the, Bonnie Bigard and, let's see, Albert Nicholson. Albert Nicholson and Bonnie Bigard. And the bass player was Jackson...

ctx.x: They had a union then but it wasn't able to.

Yeah, well the union wasn't as strong as it is now and the president wasn't the president we have now. I think Harry Gray is one of the greatest presidents we've had. I may be a little prejudiced because I served as a board of director of Local 20 years, and three years on the trial board. This was 23 consecutive years. Are you still official? No, I was defeated. I was defeated there in December. So getting back to this band, Weatherford, it lasted a little while, about four to six weeks, closed up on a Sunday…
